title: Triangle identities for the rational projective line
statement:
With $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ as in
[det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit], for
$M\in\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf P^1_Y,\Lambda))$ and $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{Rq_*M}\circ Rq_*(\eta_M)
&=Rq_*\bigl(1_M\otimes(\operatorname{Tr}_{p_1}\circ Rp_{1*}\delta_\Lambda)\bigr),\\
q^*(\varepsilon_K)(1)[2]\circ\eta_{q^*K(1)[2]}
&=1_{q^*K(1)[2]}\otimes(\operatorname{Tr}_{p_2}\circ Rp_{2*}\delta_\Lambda),
\end{aligned}
$$

and both right sides are identities. Consequently $(\eta,\varepsilon)$ is the
unit and counit of an adjunction $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ between
$\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf P^1_Y,\Lambda))$ and $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$, and
$q^!\simeq q^*(1)[2]$, with $q^!$ the right adjoint of
[sk-prop-sf-existence].

proof.text:
Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$ and $W=P\times_Y P$. Fix the notation and the canonical unit and counit of [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit]. Write $L=q^*$, $R=Rq_*$, $A=p_1^*$, $B=p_2^*$, $S=Rp_{1*}$, $U=Rp_{2*}$ and $T_Z=\Lambda_Z(1)[2]$; all tensor products below are derived. The module-object convention [sk-def-sfb-module-objects](3) gives sheaves with a $\Lambda_Z$-action, and [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives the ringed-topos pullback and direct-image formulas. The explicit comparison [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies their ordinary unbounded derived categories, tensors, pullback/direct-image functors, and the specified adjunctions and projection maps with the ringed-topos constructions. The original adjunction is [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. Here $f^*$ denotes $Lf^*$; no discrete constant-$E$ etale category is substituted.

The maps $q,p_1,p_2$ are relative projective lines, over $Y,P,P$ respectively; [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with two homogeneous coordinates makes all three proper. Hence [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] makes their canonical projection maps invertible for both arbitrary localizing factors. The unit/counit node supplies the invertible canonical exchange $\beta_M:LRM\to UAM$ and its version $\bar\beta_N:LRN\to SBN$ with the projections interchanged. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to identify $RU=RS=R(qp_i)_*$ and $S\Delta_*=U\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$. The projection/exchange equality is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], including its naturality in both factors. Define
$$b_M:LRM\otimes T_P\xrightarrow{\beta_M\otimes1}UAM\otimes T_P\xrightarrow{\mathrm{projection}}U(AM\otimes T_W).$$
The unit is $b_M^{-1}\circ U((1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)c_M)$, where $c_M:\Delta_*M\simeq AM\otimes\Delta_*\Lambda_P$ is the canonical identification in that node.

source.place: Opening paragraph: canonical maps, composition and projection/exchange coherence

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-kunneth-factorizations] to the ringed-topos self-square $(q,p_1,p_2)$ of step 1. Its two projection/exchange presentations give one map $\kappa_{M,N}:RM\otimes RN\to RU(AM\otimes BN)=RS(AM\otimes BN)$ for arbitrary localizing $M,N$. Its hypotheses use the original derived pullback/direct-image adjunctions, and do not presuppose the adjunction being proved. All its factors are invertible here by step 1.

Put $N=T_P$, $t=\operatorname{Tr}_q:RT_P\to\Lambda_Y$, and $t_1=\operatorname{Tr}_{p_1}:ST_W\to\Lambda_P$. Clause (3) of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients], applied to the separated finite-type map $q:P\to Y$, says explicitly $t_1\circ\bar\beta_{T_P}=L(t)$. In the first presentation of $\kappa$, its last two arrows are $R(b_M)$. Consequently substituting the unit and counit of [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit] expresses the first triangle as
$$Rq_*M\simeq RS\Delta_*M\xrightarrow{RS((1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)c_M)}RS(AM\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\kappa_{M,T_P}^{-1}}RM\otimes RT_P\xrightarrow{1\otimes t}RM.$$
Use the second presentation of $\kappa$ and $t_1\bar\beta_{T_P}=L(t)$. Naturality of the projection map for $q$ with respect to $t$ gives the last two arrows as
$$RS(AM\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{R(\mathrm{projection}^{-1})}R(M\otimes ST_W)\xrightarrow{R(1\otimes t_1)}RM.$$
Finally, naturality of the projection map for $p_1$ with respect to $\delta_\Lambda$ identifies the class arrow with $1_M\otimes S\delta_\Lambda$. Its source normalization is canonical: $c_M^{-1}$ is the projection map for $\Delta$, whose transpose is the identity under $\Delta^*A=\mathrm{id}$; the section normalization of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition], with $i=\Delta$, $p=p_1$, $V=\Lambda_P$, gives the identity of $M$ under $S\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$. Thus the resulting composite is exactly $Rq_*(1_M\otimes(t_1\circ Rp_{1*}\delta_\Lambda))$. This proves the first equality before using integration.

source.place: First identity: expansion of the kernel, exchange and projection square

proof.text:
For the second triangle set $M=LK\otimes T_P=q^*K(1)[2]$. The canonical comparisons give $AM=BM$, since $AL=BL$ and $AT_P=BT_P=T_W$. To check the map following the class arrow, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to $(f,f',g,g')=(q,p_2,q,p_1)$, with its $E=T_P$ and $Q=K$. In displayed factor order the resulting equality is
$$\beta_{LK\otimes T_P}\circ L(\mathrm{projection}_q)=\mathrm{projection}_{p_2}\circ(1_{LK}\otimes\beta_{T_P}):LK\otimes LRT_P\longrightarrow U(BLK\otimes T_W).$$
All projections here are invertible by [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing]. With $t=\operatorname{Tr}_q$ and $t_2=\operatorname{Tr}_{p_2}$, [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](3) gives $t_2\beta_{T_P}=L(t)$. The definition of $\varepsilon_K$ is $(1_K\otimes t)\circ\mathrm{projection}_q^{-1}$. Invert the displayed coherence equality, compose with $1_{LK}\otimes L(t)$, tensor with the outside $T_P$, and apply the tensor-associativity identity of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] for this outside factor. Naturality then gives the explicit equality
$$ (L\varepsilon_K\otimes1_{T_P})\circ b_M^{-1}=(1_M\otimes t_2)\circ\mathrm{projection}_{p_2}^{-1}:U(AM\otimes T_W)\longrightarrow M,$$
where on the right $AM$ is identified with $BM$.

source.place: Second identity: common pulled-back factor and naturality with respect to the diagonal class

proof.text:
Substitution of the unit of [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit] therefore gives the complete composite
$$M\simeq U\Delta_*M\xrightarrow{U((1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)c_M)}U(BM\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{projection}^{-1}}M\otimes UT_W\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_2}M.$$
Here $U\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$ is the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The canonical $c_M$ also equals the inverse diagonal projection with $B$ in place of $A$: their transposes are both $1_M$ under $\Delta^*A=\Delta^*B=\mathrm{id}$, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Under the $p_2$ projection its source is $M\otimes U\Delta_*\Lambda_P=M$, by the section normalization of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] for $i=\Delta$, $p=p_2$, $V=\Lambda_P$. Naturality with respect to $\delta_\Lambda$ now makes the class arrow $1_M\otimes U\delta_\Lambda$. This proves that the second composite is $1_{q^*K(1)[2]}\otimes(t_2\circ Rp_{2*}\delta_\Lambda)$. The only extra shift interchanges above move the outside degree-two Tate shift past another factor, with sign $(-1)^{2r}=1$ in degree $r$.

source.place: Second identity: diagonal normalization and class naturality after the projection/exchange computation

proof.text: The identity $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}\circ Rp_{i*}\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}=1$ for both $i=1,2$, with source $Rp_{i*}\Delta_*\mathbf Z_\ell=\mathbf Z_\ell$, is [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](2). Clauses (1) and (2) of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients] give precisely these equalities for $\Lambda=E$ and $\Qlb$, as equalities of morphisms over the pulled-back coefficient sheaf. Substitute them into steps 2–4. Tensoring an identity with $1_M$ is the identity and $Rq_*$ preserves identity maps. Both displayed triangle composites are therefore identities for every $M,K$ of the statement, with no boundedness imposed on them.

source.place: Integration identities, after the second identity

proof.text:
Write $F=Rq_*$ and $G=q^*(1)[2]$. The naturality supplied by [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit] and the two triangles just proved give the adjunction directly: send $a:M\to GK$ to $\varepsilon_K\circ F(a)$, and send $b:FM\to K$ to $G(b)\circ\eta_M$. Their composites are
$$\varepsilon_K F(G(b)\eta_M)=b\,\varepsilon_{FM}F\eta_M=b,$$
$$G(\varepsilon_KF(a))\eta_M=G\varepsilon_K\,\eta_{GK}\,a=a,$$
using naturality of $\varepsilon$ and $\eta$, respectively, and step 5. The bijections are natural in $M,K$ since these transformations and the functors are natural. The images of the identity maps are exactly the prescribed $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$. This proves $F\dashv G$ with those unit and counit.

source.place: Triangle identities exhibit the asserted adjunction; elementary Hom calculation

proof.text: To compare with Brown's right adjoint, use [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) to identify $\Loc(\Dctf(-,\Lambda))$ with $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\Lambda))$ at these field stages. The standing schemes are qcqs (finite type over a field gives quasi-compactness, and the separated diagonal is quasi-compact). The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with two homogeneous coordinates. The compactification $(\mathrm{id}_P,q)$ gives $Rq_!=Rq_*\mathrm{id}_!=Rq_*$; for the compactification chosen in [sk-prop-sf-existence], [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] supplies the comparison to this trivial one. Write this comparison as $\phi:Rq_!^{c}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*$. For $b:Rq_*M\to K$, the Brown transpose of $b\circ\phi_M$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(Rq_*M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,q^!K)$; its inverse sends a Brown adjunct $a:Rq_!^{c}M\to K$ to $a\circ\phi_M^{-1}$. These maps are natural and inverse, since $\phi$ is a natural isomorphism. In particular, if $e^{c}$ is Brown's counit, the counit for $Rq_*\dashv q^!$ is $e^c_K\circ\phi_{q^!K}^{-1}$. Thus $q^!$ and the functor $G$ of step 6 are right adjoints of the same $Rq_*$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]: the component $q^!K\to GK$ is the $G$-transpose of Brown's counit and its inverse is the $q^!$-transpose of $\varepsilon_K$. Its statement gives naturality, inverse identities and counit compatibility. Hence $q^!\simeq q^*(1)[2]$ on the stated localizing categories.

source.place: Final paragraph: trivial compactification and uniqueness of right adjoints

(1) The flagged batch-5 citation of lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison is acceptable. It is a generic comparison between module objects and ringed-topos sheaves of modules, covering the derived functors, tensor, adjunction and projection map. Neither the Poincaré duality assumption (isIso_poincareMap) nor the trace-formula assumption states it. Batch 5 already reaches it independently of this delivery, through det-thm-sf-pf-adic-projection (path from nt-target-weil-conjectures via sk-thm-sf-package, computed on the snapshot). nt-target-poincare-isiso is not reached from the batch-5 roots. The node is unsplit with proof_deps [], so citing it imports no step of either assumed proof. Its hypotheses hold here: characteristic p ≠ ℓ, separated finite-type k-schemes, and E or Q̄_ℓ as a commutative condensed ring. (2) Steps 1-7 follow the main-20261015 blueprint proof: first identity, second identity, integration, then uniqueness of the right adjoint via the trivial compactification. Base change is the canonical mate β from the unit-counit node, never a seeded theorem. Coefficients are always unbounded modules over the pulled-back condensed Λ on Loc(D_bc), identified with Loc(D_ctf) by det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc(2). I recomputed both triangles. The first presentation of κ is R(b_M)∘π_q. Using t_1β̄ = L(t) (diagonal-tower-coefficients clause 3) and π-naturality, the first triangle reduces to R(1⊗t_1)∘Rπ_{p1}^{-1}. In the unit, the unit map a_M equals the diagonal projection π_Δ, because their transposes agree. In the second triangle the coherence node applies with (q,p_2,q,p_1), E = T_P, Q = K. The two T_W factors in step 3 differ by the swap on Λ(1)[2]⊗Λ(1)[2], which is the identity. Step 5 is diagonal-tower-trace(2) plus coefficients (1)-(2); step 6 (the Hom bijection) is elementary; step 7 transports Brown's adjoint along φ in the correct direction, using det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle and det-sp-unique-right-adjoint. (3) Both new nodes are true and are not clauses of the item. In lem-sfb-ringed-kunneth-factorizations both composites have the transpose (A v_M∘θ)⊗B v_N. lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition states the standard tensor and composition coherences, and its section clause follows from them with π_id = id. Tested on identity maps, zero objects and non-cartesian squares. Neither duplicates an existing node: lem-trf-relative-kunneth-counit, def-sfb-projection-formula and prop-sf-pf-coherence are in different settings.
